rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for multimodal approaches. This experiment tests the simplest multimodal configuration (singleprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, concat fusion) to evaluate if combining modalities provides immediate performance benefits. It isolates the effect of multimodal fusion while using standard encoders, creating a reference point for comparing more complex configurations later.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieved 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It balances exploration (testing a key design choice) and exploitation (building on the multimodal baseline), while avoiding unnecessary complexity.

Existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models (config_016/017) achieve ~0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (vs previous None) to isolate the impact of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration of key design choices while building on prior multimodal success.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion (config_018) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced vision transformer) improves performance, isolating the effect of the image encoder while keeping other parameters consistent. This balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a potentially more powerful image representation.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and avgpool aggregation achieve high accuracy (0.6287). This experiment tests whether switching fusion from concat (config_024) to weighted (config_025) further improves performance, clarifying the impact of fusion strategy. It is the best use of the next experiment as it directly builds on the strongest prior result while isolating a key design choice.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve the highest accuracy (0.6352 in config_025). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation (used in config_025) with transformer aggregation could further improve performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It is a logical extension of the current top-performing configuration, balancing exploration of key design choices with exploitation of promising directions.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with pca_n2000 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_025) achieve the highest accuracy (0.6352). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while keeping other components the same (image encoder, aggregation, fusion) could improve performance. This comparison isolates the effect of the RNA encoder, a critical design choice, and leverages the strong evidence from config_025 to explore a promising direction with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows config_037 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation while retaining scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion. This clarifies whether transformer aggregation improves performance over avgpool, a critical design choice. It's a logical extension of the current best model and could reveal if more complex aggregation methods enhance accuracy further.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests if using scgpt as the RNA encoder instead of scvi_n200 can further improve accuracy, focusing on a critical design choice (RNA encoder) that could potentially outperform the current best.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile configurations with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests a similar setup using scgpt RNA encoder and concat fusion, which could isolate the impact of RNA encoder choice and fusion method. It is the best use of the final experiment to explore potential improvements in the scgpt-based pipeline.
